title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-03-16
content:
Weekly infrastructure update (week ending 2026-03-16) - GPU fleet, regions, capacity planning

Summary:
- Overall fleet health stable. No Sev1 incidents this week.
- Demand continues to trend up ~12% week-over-week driven by a few AI-native customers ramping production traffic.
- We are seeing sustained queueing on p4d-backed pools during NA business hours; follow-up action items below.

Key metrics (last 7 days):
- Fleet utilization (weighted by GPU slots): 72% avg (up from 64% last week).
- p4d instances (na-west1): 85% avg utilization during 09:00-18:00 PDT.
- A100 pools (eu-west1): 60% avg utilization.
- Peak GPU queue backlog: ~120 pending requests (peak 2026-03-12 11:34 PDT).
- Autoscaler scale-up latency (95th): 2.4m due to provisioning delays for new p4d nodes.
- Preemptible eviction rate: 6% (acceptable but tracking).

Incidents / outages:
- 2026-03-12 11:30 PDT: transient provisioning delay in na-west1 caused 15m elevated latencies for canary customers. Root cause: cloud provider API rate limit + single AZ capacity shortage. Mitigations: added retry/backoff and fallback to overflow pool in eu-west1 for latency-sensitive customers (see INFRA-4321).

Region updates:
- NA (na-west1): High demand. Working with cloud partner to reserve +2 p4d-equivalent nodes for next 2 weeks (short-term mitigation). Long-term: exploring cross-AZ stretched allocation to reduce single-AZ shortage risk.
- EU (eu-west1): Capacity healthy; shifting some non-latency-critical workloads from NA to EU overnight to balance utilization.
- APAC (ap-southeast1): Pilot completed for one customer; utilization low. No further action this sprint.

Capacity planning / forecast:
- Baseline committed capacity: 120 GPU slots across all pools.
- Forecast (next 4 weeks): demand increase 15-25% if two pending customer ramps go live (INFRA-4387).
- Recommendation: provision +8 GPU slots (p4d-equivalent) in NA in two phases: +4 this week (short-term) and +4 next sprint (after monitoring).

Autoscaling and provisioning notes:
- Scale-up latency spike correlated with pre-provisioning credit exhaustion for our burst accounts. Action: increase burst credit pool for na-west1 to cover peak hours (owned by Riley).
- Implemented retry-with-jitter in provisioner (PR: GH:redwood-infra/provisioning#742). Observed reduced failure rate in canary runs.
- Investigating faster warm-pool strategies (snapshot + quick-attach) to cut 95th scale-up to <1m.

Cost optimization:
- Evaluating shifting some eval and offline workloads to preemptible instances; estimate 22% cost savings with 4% added re-run cost.
- Discussing quantization/throughput trade-offs with ML infra (Priya) to lower per-token GPU time for background batch jobs.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Short-term reserve vs. cross-region fallback: short-term reserve reduces latency risk but increases cost; cross-region fallback adds network egress and potential latency for synchronous workloads. Default: reserve +2 p4d-equivalents and enable eu-west1 fallback for hardened routes.
- Preemptible usage threshold: target up to 30% non-latency-critical capacity. Need SLO review from product.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Aisha: Submit order to reserve +2 p4d-equivalent nodes in na-west1 (target provisioning by 2026-03-18).
- Riley: Increase burst credit pool for na-west1 and monitor scale-up latency; update by 2026-03-17.
- Priya: Run cost-vs-reliability analysis for moving batch evals to preemptible nodes; share numbers 2026-03-20.
- Liam: Implement and test warm-pool snapshot attach strategy in staging; demo 2026-03-23.
- Miguel: Draft SLO update for allowing 30% preemptible capacity for non-latency routes; review with product 2026-03-19.

Standup notes / meeting highlights:
- Infra daily standup (03/16): main ask from Platform: faster scaling for customer X canary; we agreed to enable eu-west1 fallback for the canary and prioritize p4d reservation.
- Weekly ops sync with SRE (03/15): Reviewed incident timeline and confirmed rate-limit mitigation for provider API calls.
- Cross-team: Product-Hosted-API requested clearer per-route fallback settings in the Console; we'll expose fallback region and priority flags in the next console sprint (ticket: INFRA-4403).

Risks & blockers:
- Provider AZ capacity fluctuates; our reservation requests are not guaranteed beyond short windows. Ongoing negotiation required.
- Cost vs. latency balance for sustained demand increases—need exec decision on temporary budget for reservations if ramps continue.

Notes to self / background links:
- See INFRA-4321 for incident RCA and timeline.
- Provisioning PR: GH:redwood-infra/provisioning#742 (retry + jitter).
- Capacity plan draft: CONFLUENCE:infra/gpu-capacity-plan-2026 (working draft).

Appendix (raw numbers):
- Yesterday (2026-03-15) snapshot: total slots 124, used 89, queued 42 at 11:10 PDT.
- 7-day avg GPU hours consumed: 5,840 GPU-hours (p4d-eq).

If there are no objections, I'll proceed with short-term reservation and enable eu-west1 fallback for the affected canary routes. Please add comments or tag owners on the linked JIRA tickets.

-- Aisha
